title: scoped-admin-fencing-and-hybrid-rbac-surface
creator: Maria Chen
description: Problem: Our current RBAC surface is coarse-grained and central admin roles can operate across-tenancy and across-resource families without fine-grained boundaries. This increases blast radius for misconfiguration, complicates audit trails, and blocks Private/VPC customers with tight compliance needs.
goal: Design and deliver a hybrid RBAC v2 surface that enforces scoped admin fencing: allow scoped administrative roles (team-admin, tenant-admin, region-admin) with explicit resource boundaries, and provide migration tooling plus audit hooks so every elevation and policy change is traceable.
proposed_solution: 1) Define 'scope anchors' (account, tenant, project, region, model-surface) as first-class tokens in the permission lattice. 2) Introduce 'admin-affinity' roles that are normal roles with added admin flags and an explicit scope clause. 3) Enforce a deny-by-default evaluation where explicit allow must include a scope anchor. 4) Add immutable audit log events for grant/revoke and scope changes and link those events to the token/SSO identity, session id, and justification field. 5) Provide a short CLI and Console UX to perform scoped rollouts and a migration shim to map current global-admin bindings to tenant-scoped admin or a breakglass emergency role.
design_decisions: Keep resource hierarchy explicit: account > tenant > project > deployment > model-instance
Explicit deny takes precedence over allows for cross-scope requests
Breakglass role remains available but requires JIT approval and audit metadata
Audit records are append-only and include pre/post policy states for each change
data_model_changes: roles table: add 'scope_template' column (string) to persist template e.g. 'tenant:{tenant_id}'
bindings table: add 'bound_scope_id' and 'bound_scope_type' (strings) for fast eval
policy_evaluation cache key augmented with scope-hash to prevent cross-tenant cache leakage
audit_events: new types 'ROLE_BOUND', 'ROLE_UNBOUND', 'SCOPE_ESCALATION', 'BREAKGLASS_USE' with standardized JSON payload stored as blob
migration_plan: Phase 1: Analysis script to enumerate current global-admin bindings and map them to candidate scopes using ownership heuristics (owner tags, resource prefixes). Phase 2: Create a sandbox migration that applies scoped bindings for a subset of tenants and runs synthetic authorization tests. Phase 3: Gradual migration with opt-in windows; for tenants that opt-out we create explicit 'global-admin-limited' roles with reduced surface area. Provide rollback plan to restore previous bindings and an immutable migration audit record.
acceptance_criteria: All new role creations require a scope_template; creating a global-scoped role must be gated by a config flag and documented justification
Policy evaluation test harness shows zero auth regressions for 95% of sampled production traces after migration sandbox
Console exposes scope selectors when granting admin roles and prevents ambiguous grants
Audit log exposes sufficient context to attribute every grant/revoke to an identity, session, and justification
Breakglass flows recorded and automatically revoke ephemeral elevated tokens after 1 hour unless extended by explicit approval
testing_plan: Unit tests for matcher logic, integration tests for evaluation precedence (deny > allow), property tests for caching/scoping collisions, and e2e tests using a sample tenant with synthetic load. Run a security fuzzing pass to attempt cross-tenant privilege escalation using crafted scope-hash collisions.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind 'scoped-admin-fencing' for Console/API. 2) Internal early-adopter tenants enabled for three weeks. 3) Monitor auth failure rates, admin operation latencies, and audit log size. 4) Expand to all tenants in waves with manual checkpoints and support on-call rotation for migration failures.
observability_and_metrics: alert: sudden increase in authz failures (>0.5% p50) during migration window
dashboard: 'Scoped Admin Migration' showing bound roles, orphaned global roles, and breakglass usages
security_considerations: - Ensure KMS-backed signing for audit event integrity. - Harden breakglass initiation with SSO MFA and an approver workflow. - Threat model reviewed: lateral movement via mis-bounded scopes and cache poisoning. - Require security_review_required before GA.
open_questions: What is the maximum number of scope anchors to support without blowing up policy combinatorics?
Do we allow wildcard scopes for delegated service accounts? If so, how to audit their use?
How will enterprise customers with thousands of tenants want to author roles (templates vs. UI)?
